Hi Claire — attaching a concise matrix and a simplified dataflow diagram. Long-form notes below; please let us know if you want this signed and we can push to DocuSign.

Quick summary (hosted API):
- Primary subprocessors that may touch customer payloads:
  * Google Cloud LLC (Compute & Storage) — us-east1 / europe-west1 as applicable; role: compute execution, ephemeral storage
  * VaultKey Systems (VaultCorp) — managed KMS for our hosted control plane (keys stored in US by default; EU-keying can be configured under Dedicated/Private contracts)
  * EdgeCache Inc. — global CDN for model artifacts and model shard distribution (regional POPs; no customer payload caching beyond short-lived artifact caches)
  * Observability vendor (TraceSight) — metrics/traces (no PII in traces; sample-level telemetry; EU tenancy available)

- Transitive dependencies and OSS:
  * Tokenizer libraries (open-source) — not subprocessors; no network calls to third parties.
  * Model downloader component calls public model registries (open repos) to pull weights during onboarding — weights are stored in our artifact store (region pinned per deployment when possible). If a customer uses the hosted plan and selects a non-pinned model, model artifacts may be pulled from third-party registries that are subject to that registry's export controls.

- Export-control notes:
  * Most user payloads and open-source libraries fall under standard EAR classifications (e.g., EAR99).
  * Model weights may have restrictions depending on the upstream provider/license; we flag any non-EAR99 models during onboarding and surface to the customer. For MedSupply, if you require explicit export-control attestation for specific model origins, we can include that in the onboarding checklist.

- EU data residency:
  * Hosted API: control plane and some artifact handling default to US regions; customer request can trigger regional pinning for artifacts and ephemeral compute. Hosted customers in EU should expect some control-plane metadata (billing/metrics) to be processed in the US unless on a Dedicated/Private contract.
  * Dedicated / Private: full regional pinning available (we offer EU-only deployments with KMS in-region).

- Restricted jurisdictions:
  * None of our vendor contracts or POPs are operated out of Russia/Belarus. We do not route customer payloads through those countries.

Attachments: redwood-export-control-subprocessor-matrix.xlsx, dataflow-region-map-v2.png, sig-lite-answers.pdf

If you want a one-sentence procurement attestation we can provide: "Redwood Inference confirms the attached subprocessor matrix and the current export-control and dataflow posture for our hosted offering; additional regional pinning is available under Dedicated/Private contracts."

Cheers,
